title: Phase transitions and microphases in elastomers. II. Anisotropy-driven morphologies
authors: Manu Mannattil, David Andelman, Haim Diamant
abstract: In swollen elastomers, elasticity can arrest macroscopic demixing between the polymer network and the solvent, producing stable domains of finite size. While previous theories have focused on isotropically swollen elastomers, anisotropy strongly influences the phase behavior of many related systems, such as gels and crosslinked polymer blends. Building on the approach developed in Part I of this two-part paper, we investigate the effects of two experimentally induced sources of anisotropy: uniaxial swelling and stiffness gradients. We show that uniaxial swelling can lead to the formation of stable lamellar microphases and modify phase behavior, while stiffness gradients can cause spatial variations in the characteristic microphase size.
summary: This work theoretically examines how mechanical anisotropy, induced by uniaxial swelling or stiffness gradients, dictates the phase behavior and resulting microstructures in swollen elastomers. By coupling Ginzburg-Landau theory with linearized elastic energy, the authors predict the formation of specific microphases and quantify how external mechanical fields modify these transitions.
main_problem: The paper investigates how mechanical anisotropy influences the phase transitions and resulting microphase morphologies in swollen elastomers.
main_result: Uniaxial swelling can stabilize lamellar microphases whose orientation depends on the applied stretch, and stiffness gradients cause spatial variations in the characteristic microphase domain size.
method: The analysis uses a free energy functional approach, linearizing the elastic energy and deriving an effective free energy in terms of the order parameter, followed by stability analysis in Fourier space.
model_or_system: The system is swollen elastomers modeled by a crosslinked polymer network and solvent. The free energy combines a Ginzburg-Landau term with an elastic energy term derived from the nonlinear elastic energy.
key_observables: Microphase separation temperature (Tm), bulk instability temperature (T0), and the characteristic microphase domain size.
important_parameters: Anisotropy factor (p), Elastocapillary Number (gamma_0), and the wavevector dependence of the longitudinal modulus (M_q).
main_assumptions: The system is assumed to be at thermodynamic equilibrium in an affinely deformed state, and the elastic energy is linearized to quadratic order in the displacement field.
figures_summary: The paper discusses a phase diagram showing the stability of lamellar microphases in the plane of the anisotropy factor (p) and the elastocapillary number (gamma_0).
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous work (Part I), first deriving the total free energy functional by combining Ginzburg-Landau and linearized elastic energies. It then analyzes the effects of uniaxial swelling and stiffness gradients by examining the resulting wavevector-dependent moduli and stability criteria.
why_interesting: While focused on soft matter, the methodology of coupling phase separation (order parameter dynamics) with mechanical constraints (elastic energy) is relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and pattern formation in complex systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
